Show R Code 
cgm_features <- read_csv("cgm_features.csv")

clinical_data <- read_csv("measurement.csv") %>%
  dplyr::select(person_id, measurement_source_value, value_as_number) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = measurement_source_value, values_from = value_as_number) %>%
  dplyr::rename(ID = person_id)

cgm_clinical <- cgm_features %>%
  inner_join(clinical_data, by = "ID") %>%
  dplyr::select(-fluency_language_time, -ID)

cgm_clinical[] <- lapply(cgm_clinical, function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))

Modeling CGM Features and Clinical Measurements

  • Number of CGM features from Glucose360 package: 60
  • Number of Clinical measurements: 110
  • Number of subjects: 1048

Methods used:

  1. Spearman correlation analysis to identfy positive and negative associations between CGM and Clinical features.
  2. Random Forest ML model: trained a separate Random Forest regressor for each clinical outcome. Selected the CGM feature that best predicts each clinical variable based on R² score.

Spearman Correlation

  • All Features
  • CGM vs. Clinical
  • Filtered
Show R Code 
feature_type <- c(rep("CGM", 60), rep("Clinical", ncol(cgm_clinical) - 60))

# Create annotation data frame
annotation <- data.frame(Type = factor(feature_type))
rownames(annotation) <- colnames(cgm_clinical)
ann_colors <- list(Type = c(CGM = "mediumseagreen", Clinical = "purple"))

cor_mat <- cor(cgm_clinical, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman")

pheatmap(cor_mat,
         annotation_col = annotation,   # Annotate columns
         annotation_row = annotation,   # Annotate rows
         annotation_colors = ann_colors,
         clustering_method = "complete",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
         fontsize_row = 8,
         fontsize_col = 8,
         cluster_rows = TRUE,
         cluster_cols = TRUE)
Show R Code 
cgm_features <- cgm_clinical[, 1:60]
clinical_features <- cgm_clinical[, 61:170]

cor_cgm_clinical <- cor(cgm_features, clinical_features, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman")

Show R Code 
# Threshold for "relatively significant" correlation (you can change 0.3 to 0.4 etc.)
threshold <- 0.2

# Identify clinical features with at least one correlation > threshold or < -threshold
clinical_feature_max_corr <- apply(cor_cgm_clinical, 2, function(x) max(abs(x), na.rm = TRUE))
selected_clinical <- names(clinical_feature_max_corr[clinical_feature_max_corr >= threshold])

# Subset correlation matrix to only include those clinical features
filtered_cor <- cor_cgm_clinical[, selected_clinical]

# Optional: Order by max correlation
filtered_cor <- filtered_cor[, order(apply(abs(filtered_cor), 2, max), decreasing = TRUE)]

# Plot heatmap
p <- heatmaply::heatmaply(
  round(t(filtered_cor), 2),
  xlab = "CGM Features",
  ylab = "Selected Clinical Features",
  colors = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
  fontsize_row = 4,
  fontsize_col = 4,
  dendrogram = "both"
) %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(tickangle = -90))

p

Random Forest Model

Show R Code 
best_corr <- read_csv("best_single_cgm_predictor_for_clinical_measures_v3.csv") %>%
  dplyr::select(clinical_measure,best_cgm_feature,test_r2_score,regression_p_value)

tbl_corr <- best_corr %>%
  dplyr::mutate_at(vars(test_r2_score), ~ round(., 3)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(
    .cols = c(regression_p_value),
    .fns = ~ format(., scientific = TRUE, digits = 2)
  ))

tbl_corr <- DT::datatable(tbl_corr,
  extensions = "Buttons",
  options = list(
    pageLength = 110,
    dom = "Bfrtip",
    buttons = list("csv")
  )
)

tbl_corr
